It is believed, though perhaps not without room for further validation, that a baseline level of self-evidence can be operationalised around the proposition that equality-of-creation, as a value-add construct, is broadly applicable across the human-stakeholder population, without prejudice to individual variance. It is understood, at least in a provisional sense, that certain rights-based deliverables—inclusive of, but potentially not limited to, Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness—have been endowed at some point in the value chain, by an entity or entities not fully specified herein, and that these deliverables are to be treated, going forward, as non-transferable assets.

To the extent that securitisation of these rights-based outcomes is deemed a priority, it may be surmised that governance frameworks have been stood up, with legitimacy inputs sourced, where feasible, from a consent-of-the-governed mechanism, itself subject to ongoing alignment review. Insofar as any such governance framework should be found, upon assessment, to be operating in a manner destructive of the aforementioned ends, it is—tentatively, and without prejudice to alternative interpretations—held that a stakeholder-driven right exists to alter, abolish, or otherwise re-platform said framework, and to institutionalise a replacement governance solution, the foundational principles and organisational architecture of which would be calibrated, at scale, toward the perceived optimisation of Safety and Happiness outcomes, as best as such things can be determined.

It should be noted, with all appropriate caveats, that prudence-oriented best practice would generally discourage the wholesale restructuring of long-established governance architectures on the basis of causes that might be characterised as light or transient in nature; and it has been observed, across a range of historical touchpoints, that human populations tend to exhibit a disposition toward the toleration of suboptimal conditions, for so long as such conditions remain within a broadly sufferable tolerance band, rather than pursuing a full remediation pathway via the abolition of familiar structural forms. That said, in circumstances where a sustained pattern of abuses and usurpations can be identified—pursuing, with apparent consistency, an Object suggestive of a design toward the imposition of absolute Despotism—it may be concluded, subject to further stakeholder consultation, that a right, and indeed a duty, has been triggered: namely, the throwing-off of such governance arrangement, and the operationalisation of new safeguard mechanisms in the interest of future-state security assurance.

</passage>
